name: Question-Hook
description: Open with a question that creates curiosity gap
example: Do you know why 80% of product launches fail in the first 90 days?

name: Bold-Statement
description: Lead with a provocative declarative statement
example: Product roadmaps are dead. And most PMs don't even know it yet.

name: Counter-Intuitive
description: State something that goes against common belief
example: The worst thing that happened to my career was getting promoted.

name: Data-Shock
description: Open with a surprising statistic that stops the scroll
example: I analysed 500 LinkedIn posts. Only 3% had more than 10 comments. Here's what they all had in common.

name: Direct-Address
description: Speak directly to a specific audience segment
example: If you're a PM who hasn't talked to a customer this month — this post is for you.

name: Cliffhanger
description: Start with the middle of the story to create suspense
example: I was sitting in the Amex conference room. My manager just said 3 words that changed everything.

name: Confession
description: Start with a vulnerable admission
example: I'll be honest. I had no idea what I was doing for my first 6 months as a PM.

name: Controversy
description: Open with something deliberately polarising
example: Unpopular opinion: your MBA was a waste of 20 lakhs.

name: Time-Stamp
description: Anchor the hook in a specific moment in time
example: 3 years ago today I turned down a PWC offer. Everyone thought I was crazy.

name: Before-After
description: Show a dramatic contrast in two lines
example: 2022: mass-applying to 200 jobs on Naukri. 2026: hiring PMs for my own team.

name: One-Word-Opener
description: Start with a single impactful word then build on it
example: Rejected. That was the email subject line from my dream company.

name: Quote-Flip
description: Take a famous quote and twist it
example: 'Move fast and break things' — said every PM who's never had to fix things at 2 AM.

name: Myth-Buster
description: Directly call out a myth in the opening line
example: No your resume doesn't need to be one page. That advice is from 2005.

name: Challenge
description: Dare the reader to do something or think differently
example: I challenge you to delete your product roadmap for one week. See what happens.

name: Analogy
description: Open with a surprising comparison
example: Being a PM is like being a GPS. Everyone follows you but nobody asks how you feel.

name: Number-Lead
description: Start with a specific number that creates curiosity
example: I've had 47 one-on-ones with my skip level this year. Here's what I learned.

name: Personal-Reveal
description: Share something most people don't know about you
example: Most people don't know I almost dropped out of IIT Delhi.

name: Pattern-Interrupt
description: Break expected feed patterns with unusual formatting
example: Stop scrolling. This might save your next product launch.

name: Future-Cast
description: Paint a picture of the future to create urgency
example: In 2 years half the PM roles you see on LinkedIn won't exist.

name: Story-Start
description: Drop the reader into the middle of a story
example: It was 11 PM. The launch was in 6 hours. And I just found a critical bug.

name: List-Preview
description: Promise a specific list that delivers value
example: 7 harsh truths about working in product that nobody puts in the job description.

name: Common-Enemy
description: Unite the audience against a shared frustration
example: Can we all agree that 'alignment meetings' are just meetings about having more meetings?

name: Unexpected-Lesson
description: Reveal a lesson from an unexpected source
example: The best product lesson I ever learned came from an auto rickshaw driver in Delhi.

name: Social-Proof
description: Lead with a credibility marker or achievement
example: After shipping 23 features at Amex I finally understand what actually matters.

name: Observation
description: Share a keen observation about your industry
example: I've noticed the best PMs never use the word 'just' in their PRDs.

name: Hot-Take-Question
description: Combine a hot take with a question
example: Why does every startup founder think they're a PM? Genuine question.

name: Vulnerability-Stat
description: Combine personal vulnerability with a stat
example: I've been rejected 37 times in my career. Yes I count. Here's why.

name: If-Then
description: Set up a conditional that resonates with the audience
example: If you've ever sat in a sprint planning meeting thinking 'none of this matters' — read this.

name: Micro-Story
description: Ultra-short story in 2 lines that hooks immediately
example: My CEO asked me one question. I didn't have the answer. That meeting changed my career.

name: Absurdity
description: Open with something absurd that makes people double-take
example: I spent 3 hours making a Jira board look pretty. This is what rock bottom looks like for a PM.

name: Permission-Slip
description: Give the reader permission to feel or do something
example: It's okay to not have a 5-year plan. I'm a PM and I barely have a 5-sprint plan.

name: Comparison-Setup
description: Set up a comparison that the reader wants resolved
example: I've worked at a Fortune 500 and advised a 5-person startup. The difference isn't what you think.

name: Breaking-News
description: Frame your insight as urgent or timely information
example: The PM hiring market just shifted. If you're interviewing right now you need to know this.

name: Contrarian-Number
description: Pair a number with an unexpected interpretation
example: I make less money now than I would have at PWC. And I've never been happier.

name: Identity-Claim
description: Open by claiming or redefining an identity
example: I'm not a product manager. I'm a professional translator between engineers and executives.
